source.author: verg
source.text: at simul heroum laudes et facta parentis iam legere et quae sit poteris cognoscere virtus, molli paulatim flavescet campus arista, incultisque rubens pendebit sentibus uva, et durae quercus sudabunt roscida mella Pauca tamen suberunt priscae vestigia fraudis, quae temptare Thetim ratibus, quae cingere muris oppida, quae iubeant telluri infindere sulcos:
source.text_original: at simul heroum laudes et facta parentis / iam legere et quae sit poteris cognoscere virtus, / molli paulatim flavescet campus arista, / incultisque rubens pendebit sentibus uva, / et durae quercus sudabunt roscida mella / Pauca tamen suberunt priscae vestigia fraudis, / quae temptare Thetim ratibus, quae cingere muris / oppida, quae iubeant telluri infindere sulcos: /
source.text_english: But as soon as you are able to read the praises and deeds of heroes and of your father, and to know what virtue is, then the plain will gradually grow golden with tender stalks, the grape, red on untended thorn-bushes, will hang, and the hard oaks will drip dewy honey. Yet there will still remain a few traces of the old cunning: the art that would bid men test Thetis with ships, that would bid them wall cities with walls, that would bid them cleave furrows into the earth.

reuse.text: tunc et molli paulatim flauescet campus arista incultisque rubens pendebit sentibus uua et durae quercus sudabunt roscida mella.
reuse.text_original: tunc et molli paulatim flauescet campus arista incultisque rubens pendebit sentibus uua et durae quercus sudabunt roscida mella.
reuse.text_english: Then too the field will gradually grow yellow with tender grain, and the grape, blushing on its uncultivated briars, will hang there, and the hard oaks will drip dewy honey.
